content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 26. Supplemental: SEI tradeoff analysis concepts. This unit focuses on scalability mechanisms.

Scalability is the ability to handle increased load by adding resources, changing allocation, or reducing work. Common mechanisms include caching, partitioning, replication, asynchronous processing, load balancing, and horizontal scaling.

Each mechanism has tradeoffs. Caching can improve latency but create staleness. Partitioning can increase capacity but complicate queries. Replication can improve availability but create consistency challenges.
Studio: pick two scalability mechanisms for a messaging app and describe the tradeoff each introduces.

concepts.name: Scalability
concepts.description: The ability of a system to maintain acceptable service as workload or data volume grows.

concepts.name: Horizontal scaling
concepts.description: Adding more instances or nodes to increase capacity rather than making one node larger.

concepts.name: Caching
concepts.description: Storing reusable data closer to consumers to reduce latency, load, or repeated computation.

concepts.name: Partitioning
concepts.description: Dividing data, work, or responsibility across multiple elements to improve scale or isolation.
